submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on a time-unit noun (year(s), month(s), week(s), day(s), season, decade, hour, also game(s)/time when used as a count of periods) that closes a span phrase measuring how long a status, trend, ranking or record has held, as in news/statistics framing: 'for the third consecutive year', 'lowest level in four years', 'first sighting in 26 years', 'stock fell for a fifth day', 'was top for three years'. It stays at zero on every other token (no floor on any prompt), on non-time nouns in the same slot ('in 26 rooms'), and on plain durations of a personal activity or age/time-reference uses ('lived there for three years', 'lasted two hours', '26 years old', 'next year', 'years ago' outside a record context).
